articles.text: LIÁNG LÌ: Kēlǐhàn Nǚshì, nín háishi gǎnhuílai le!
LIÁNG LÌ: Ms. Colihan, you made it back after all!
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Shíjiān zài jǐn, wǒ yě děi gǎnhuílai cānguān Shǒudū Gāngtiě Gōngsī a!
MS. COLIHAN: No matter how pressed I was for time, I had to get back in time to visit the Capital Iron and Steel Company!
LIÁNG LÌ: Wǒ xiǎng, nǐmen zhèicì dào Dōngběi cānguān, yào qùde dìfang nàme duō, shíjiān yídìng hěn jǐnzhāng, dàgài zhèi liǎngtiān hái huíbulái. Méi xiǎngdào, ānpáide hái bú cuò.

LIÁNG LÌ: I thought there were so many places you wanted to go on this trip to Manchuria that you would be very rushed and wouldn't be able to get back by today or tomorrow. I'm surprised it was so well arranged.

KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Ǹg, Dōngběi fāngmiàn gǎode hěn hǎo, wǒmen cānguānde dìfang jiāotōng dōu hěn fāngbian. Yánzhe tiělù, gōnglù, yízhàn yízhàn cānguānguoqu, zhème duō rénde cānguāntuán, shénme wèntí dōu méiyou fāshēng, dàjiā dōu hěn mǎnyì, zhēn shi gǎode bú cuò.

MS. COLIHAN: Yeah. The people in Manchuria did quite a good job. Every place we visited, transportation was convenient. Visiting each stop along the railroad and highway, with a tour group of that size, no problems came up, and everyone was very pleased. It was really well handled.
LIÁNG LÌ: Nín tài kèqi le.
LIÁNG LÌ: It's so nice of you to say that.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Bú shi kèqi, zhèi shi zhēnde. Duì le, zhèicì lǚxíng, wǒ hái fāxiànle yíjiàn hěn yǒu yìside shìr.
MS. COLIHAN: I'm not just saying it, it's the truth! Oh yes, I found out something very interesting during the trip.
LIÁNG LÌ: Shénme shìr a?
LIÁNG LÌ: What?

KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Péi wǒmen cānguānde yíwèi nǚ gōngzuò rényuán, cóngqián zài yíge rénmín gōngshè zuò shèyuán, hòulái hái zài yíge gōngchǎng zuò gōngren, liǎngnián yǐqián kāishǐ zài Lǚxíngshè gōngzuò, tā zhēn shi yíwèi hǎo dǎoyóu.

MS. COLIHAN: A woman on the staff that accompanied us on the trip used to be a commune member, then became a worker in a factory, and then started to work in the Travel Service two years ago. She's really a great guide.
LIÁNG LÌ: Tā shì bu shì Hēilóngjiāng rén?
LIÁNG LÌ: Is she a native of Hēilóngjiāng?
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Bú shì, tā bú shi Hēilóngjiāng rén, kěshi tā duì nàrde qíngkuàng hái zhēn shúxī. Lìshǐ, wénhuà, gōngyè, nóngyè, shénme tā dōu zhīdao. Tīng tā tánqilai zhēn yǒu yìsi.
MS. COLIHAN: No, she's not a native of Hēilóngjiāng, but she really knows the place well. History, culture, industry, agriculture, you name it. She's very interesting to listen to.
LIÁNG LÌ: Wǒ zhīdao tā shi shéi le, tā cóngqián shi qìchē zhìzàochǎngde gōngren, xiànzài shi Lǚxíngshède xiānjìn gōngzuòzhě. Tā jiào Jīn Xiǎoméi.
LIÁNG LÌ: I know who she is. She used to be a worker in an automobile manufacturing plant, and now she's one of the Travel Service's advanced workers. Her name is Jīn Xiǎoméi.

KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Duì le, duì le. Nǐ zhè yí shuō wǒ dào xiǎngqilai le, yǒu yìtiān wǒmen zuòde nèibù qìchē huàile, dàjiā dōu hěn dānxīn, wǒmen xiǎng wǒmen yídìng gǎnbushang cānguān le. Kěshi nèiwèi xiānjìn gōngzuòzhě hé jǐge rén zài qìchē xiàbianr mángle yìhuǐr, bú dào shífēn zhōng ba, chē jiù xiūhǎo le!

MS. COLIHAN: Right, right. That reminds me, one day our bus broke down, and everyone was very worried. We didn't think we could possibly make it in time for our tour. But that advanced worker worked under the bus for a while with some other people, and in less than ten minutes the bus was fixed!
LIÁNG LÌ: Suǒyǐ nèitiān nǐmen háishi àn yóulǎn jìhua, yào qùde dìfang dōu qù le?
LIÁNG LÌ: So that day, you still made it to all the places you were supposed to go, according to your tour schedule?

KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Shì a. Wǒ yǒu shíhour jiù xiǎng, zhèiwèi Jīn Xiǎoméi zhēn shi xiāngdāng cōngmingde rén, tā zěnme bú qù shàng dàxué ne? Shì bu shì Wénhuà Dà Gémìngde shíhou yǒu shénme shìqing gǎocuò le?
MS. COLIHAN: Yes. Sometimes I think to myself, this Jīn Xiǎoméi is really quite a smart person, why doesn't she go to college? Did she do something wrong during the Cultural Revolution?
LIÁNG LÌ: Ō, méi shénme shìqing. Xiànzài bù guǎn zài nǎr gōngzuò dōu yǒu hěn duō jīhui niàn shū.
LIÁNG LÌ: Oh, no. Now, no matter where you work, you have a lot of opportunities to study.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Ō, shì ma?
MS. COLIHAN: Oh, really?
LIÁNG LÌ: Shì a, bǐfang shuō, wǒmen jīntian yào cānguānde zhèige gāngtiě gōngsī ba, lǐngdǎo hàozhào zhígōng zài yèyú shíjiān xuéxí jìshu.
LIÁNG LÌ: Sure. For example, the iron and steel company that we're going to visit today: the leaders appeal to the workers and staff to study technology in their spare time.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Yǒu hěn duō rén cānjiā ma?
MS. COLIHAN: Are there a lot of people taking part?
LIÁNG LÌ: Yǒu. Jīnnián zài yèdàxué xuǎn kède zhígōng děngyú Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐqiánde liǎng-sānbèi.
LIÁNG LÌ: Yes. The number of staff and workers taking classes at evening universities this year is equal to two or three times the number before the Cultural Revolution.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Qíngkuàng hěn hǎo a! Nàme Wénhuà Dà Gémìngde shíhou ne? Yǒu méiyou yèdàxué a?
MS. COLIHAN: That's good! And what about during the Cultural Revolution? Were there evening universities then?
LIÁNG LÌ: Nèi shíhou, zhěnggèr guójiā dōu děi gǎode luànqībāzāo le, hái yǒu shénme yèdàxué a!
LIÁNG LÌ: Back then, the whole country was messed up. Evening universities? Hardly!
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Xiànzài hǎo le.
MS. COLIHAN: Now it's better.
LIÁNG LÌ: Xiànzài hǎoduō le, gōngsī yǒu shítáng, yǒu yòu'éryuán, niánqīng gōngren bú yòng shuō le, jiù shi yǒu háizide zhígōng yě yǒu tiáojiàn shàng dàxué la!
LIÁNG LÌ: Much better. The company has dining halls and kindergartens. Not only young workers, even staff and workers with children are able to take evening university courses.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Zěnme, gōngsīde zhígōng dōu zhù zài gōngsī sùshèli ma?
MS. COLIHAN: What? The staff and workers of the company all live in company housing?
LIÁNG LÌ: Shǒudū Gāngtiě Gōngsī bǐ yíge xiǎo chéng hái dà, bǎifēn zhī qībāshí yǐshàngde zhígōng hé jiāshǔ dōu zhù zài gōngsīde sùshèli, shàng, xià bān fāngbian, shēnghuó fāngbian.

LIÁNG LÌ: The Capital Iron and Steel Company is even bigger than a town. More than seventy or eighty percent of the staff and workers and their families live in company housing. It makes it more convenient to go to work and to get home from work, and makes daily life more convenient.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Nà hǎo, nà zhēn kěyi yǒu shíjiān niàn yìdiǎnr shū le.
MS. COLIHAN: That's good. Then they really have time to study.
LIÁNG LÌ: Suǒyǐ cōngmingde, nǔlì xuéxíde niánqīngrén yídìng yǒu bànfǎ niàn shūde.
LIÁNG LÌ: So the smart young people who work hard are assured of the chance to go to school.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Duì. Ǹg, wǒ hái yǒu yíge wèntí.
MS. COLIHAN: Right. Uh, I have another question.
LIÁNG LÌ: Shénme wèntí?
LIÁNG LÌ: What?
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Wǒ hǎoxiàng zài bàoshang háishi zài nǎr kànjianguo yìpiān wénzhāng, shuō Chángjiāng fùjìn, ō, Chángjiāng yǐnán yě yǒu yíge xiàndàihuàde gāngtiě gōngsī, bǐ Shǒudū Gāngtiě Gōngsī hái dà.

MS. COLIHAN: I remember seeing an article, I think in the newspaper or somewhere, that said that in the Yangtze River area, no, to the south of the Yangtze, there is another modern iron and steel company that's even larger than the Capital Iron and Steel Company.
LIÁNG LÌ: Shì a.
LIÁNG LÌ: Right.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Chángjiāng yǐnán shi zhòngyàode nóngyèqū, cóng fāzhǎn jīngjìshang kàn, hǎoxiàng yǒu yìdiǎnr bú tài héshì.
MS. COLIHAN: The area to the south of the Yangtze is an important agricultural area; from the point of view of economic development it doesn't seem to be too appropriate.
LIÁNG LÌ: Duì, gōngyè wūrǎn duì nóngyè fāzhǎn méiyou hǎochu, wǒmen zài xiǎng bànfǎ. Shǒudū Gāngtiě Gōngsī yě yǒu wūrǎnde wèntí, nǐ zhīdao, zhòng gōngyè duì shǒudū lái shuō kě bú tài héshì.

LIÁNG LÌ: Right. Industrial pollution isn't good for agricultural development. We're working on it. The Capital Iron and Steel Company also has a pollution problem. Heavy industry isn't very appropriate for a capital city, you know.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Nàme nǐde yìsi shi, Běijīng bù zhǔnbèi zài fāzhǎn zhòng gōngyè le.
MS. COLIHAN: Then you mean that Běijīng isn't planning to develop their heavy industry any further?
LIÁNG LÌ: Duì, zhèi yìdiǎn, zhèngfǔde juédìng shi hěn qīngchude, wǒmen děi bǎ Běijīng jiànshèchéng yíge yǒu wénhuà, shēnghuó fāngbian, jīngjì fādá, yòu fēicháng gānjìngde chéngshì.
LIÁNG LÌ: Right. On this point, the government's decision is very clear. We should build Běijīng into a cultural city, convenient to live in, economically developed--and very clean.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Hǎo, wǒ xiǎng wǒ xiànzài bǐjiào qīngchu le.
MS. COLIHAN: Okay, I think I understand better now.
LIÁNG LÌ: Èi, Kēlǐhàn Nǚshì, wǒ zhèr hái yǒu liǎngyàng shuǐguǒ, wǒmen bǎ ta xiāomiè le ba!
LIÁNG LÌ: Oh, Ms. Colihan, I still have a couple of fruits here, let's polish them off!
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: "Xiāomiè" le? Hǎo, hǎo. Wǒ dào shi dìyīcì tīngjian zhèige shuōfǎr.
MS. COLIHAN: "Polish them off?" Ohhh. That's the first time I've ever heard that expression.
LIÁNG LÌ: Kuài yào dào le, shuǐguǒ bù qīng ne, cānguānde shíhou názhe ta duō lèi ya, háishi xiànzài bǎ ta chīle hǎo.
LIÁNG LÌ: We're almost there. The fruit is kind of heavy. It would be a bother to carry it around while we tour. It would be better to eat it now.
KĒLǏHÀN NǙSHÌ: Hǎo, nà jiù xièxie le.
MS. COLIHAN: All right, then thank you.
